messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Multiple BGP session resets observed for customer ACME over PrivateConnect (eu-central-1b) — potential packet loss and route withdrawal. Severity: P2. Pager sent to oncall-alex.

oncall-alex: Seeing the pager. Jumping in. Anyone already on the link?

sre-ryan: I started looking — telemetry shows BGP peer 10.10.20.1 flapping at ~every 30s, routes being withdrawn then re-advertised. Route-flap dampening counts increasing.

eng-net-jess: Thanks Ryan. Can you paste the show output? I want to see the AS path and any recent config pushes.

sre-ryan: Pasted below: ```
BGP neighbor 10.10.20.1 is up
  BGP version 4, remote AS 64512, local AS 64510
  Last reset 00:00:32, 5 resets in 00:02:30
  Prefixes received: 1200
  Advertised to peer: 1187
  Route refresh: supported
```

custops-mike: Customer reports intermittent failures to their internal services (DB replication lag). They said it started ~09:12 UTC.

oncall-alex: Marking customer impact: yes (packet loss, control-plane instability). Notify customer channel and open bridge. @support-lina can you create bridge and ping the customer?

support-lina: Bridge created: https://meet.company/bridge/ACME-1749998888 — invited ACME netops. Ping request sent.

eng-platform-omar: Noted some recent infra change: yesterday at 02:00 we rolled a config that tightened BGP MD5 and updated route-maps for egress. Could that have caused asymmetric filtering?

eng-net-jess: Possible. Ask customer if they applied any changes recently. Meanwhile, temp mitigation: we can blackhole-route dampening for this peer to prevent withdrawals from affecting traffic, or add a static backup path to keep flows alive. Which option preferred?

custops-mike: Customer hasn't changed config. They confirm nothing on their side. Their edge shows the peer flapping too.

oncall-alex: Let's do a quick, low-risk mitigation: disable flap damping for this neighbor and add a static less-preferred route via secondary path so sessions remain. Prepare commands.

sre-ryan: Commands I'll run (dry run first): ```
# Disable flap damping for peer 10.10.20.1
no bgp dampening ip 10.10.20.1
# Add static route pointing to secondary transit
ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.20.30.1 250
```

eng-net-jess: Before you run, capture tcpdump on the IX interface to confirm if we see BFD or link-level flaps: `tcpdump -i ix0 host 10.10.20.1 and port 179`

sre-ryan: tcpdump shows TCP 3-way close and re-open with RSTs at the timestamps matching BGP resets. No obvious L2 carrier drops.

oncall-alex: That points to either BGP session mismatch (MD5 TTL issues) or something tearing the TCP session. Try restarting the peer with a graceful reset and disable damping. Ryan, apply config changes during quiet window now. Notify channel before change.

sre-ryan: Applying change now: disabling damping for peer and inserting static backup. Will monitor.

incident-bot: Change pushed to routers-nyc-core-3 by sre-ryan at 09:26 UTC — audit id 8f7a3c.

eng-net-jess: After change, BGP resets reduced to 0 in last 5m. Routes stabilized. Customer confirms DB replication recovered.

custops-mike: ACME says replication lag dropped back to normal. Thanks.

oncall-alex: Good. Keep monitoring for 30m, then decide on permanent fix. We should roll back temporary static route if not needed. Also open a post-incident ticket to review the MD5/TTL and route-map changes.

eng-platform-omar: I'll look into the config rolled yesterday that tightened MD5 settings — maybe we accidentally introduced a mismatch with some older peers.

eng-net-jess: Filing follow-up items: 1) Validate MD5/TCP-MSS between peers 2) Audit recent route-map changes for attribute rewriting 3) Add better telemetry for BGP RST reasons.

oncall-alex: Handoff to next oncall in 30m. @sre-ryan please add notes to the incident doc and ping the network lead if we see recurrence.

sre-ryan: Notes added to incident tracker: https://internal/incidents/1749998888 — flagged as P2, mitigated, root cause under investigation.

support-lina: Customer bridge closed at their request. They want an email summary — I'll draft and send.

eng-net-jess: @oncall-alex if stability holds we'll schedule a config rollback of the static route and coordinate a controlled MD5 tweak with ACME.

oncall-alex: Copy. Leaving channel but will be reachable. Handoff to oncall next: @sre-ryan taking golden-hour. :white_check_mark:

sre-ryan: Taking over monitoring. If I see BGP resets > 1/min I'll escalate to eng-net.

incident-bot: Incident 1749998888 moved to monitoring. Closed-bridge at 09:48 UTC.

oncall-alex: Thanks team.
